A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G2RPO research despite retitling and reformatting. Their text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Flux.1-dev alignment experiments, quantitative comparisons, granularity ablations, inference-step evaluations and generated-image comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds UniGenBench++ evaluation, a controlled visual ablation and additional generated examples.

M1.justification: Singular Stochastic Sampling, multi-granularity rollouts, summed advantages and the GRPO objective remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 corrects the post-SDE condition from t > k to t < k, matching the procedure already described in v1's prose rather than establishing a different method.

E1.justification: v3 adds UniGenBench++ evaluation alongside the retained HPSv2 training and testing coverage. Its dedicated evaluations of world knowledge, logical reasoning, grammar, composition, layout, text and other dimensions substantially broaden the tested semantic requirements (Section 7, Table 5).

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Flux.1-dev, DanceGRPO, MixGRPO and the G2RPO variant without MGAI. Table 5 extends this existing comparator set to the added benchmark. Flow-GRPO remains unevaluated; v3 adds an explanation for its exclusion.

E3.justification: Sections 7–8 introduce supplemental scoring with UniGenBench-EvalModel-qwen-72b-v1 and an eight-pair visual comparison controlling prompts and random seeds. The existing HPSv2 split, backbone, group size and sampling-step budget are retained. Newly stated shared comparator settings do not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing component/granularity ablations and 10/20-step robustness evaluation remain. v3 adds eight matched visual pairs testing MGAI's effects on texture and global structure (Figure 5), with complementary component comparisons across the new benchmark's dimensions in Table 5.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly discloses random seed 42 and sampler seed 1223627; Section 8 specifies matching random seeds within visual-ablation pairs. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests, and these disclosures do not demonstrate additional runs.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. New Table 5 substantially extends the results: UniGenBench++ overall scores are 69.21 for G2RPO, 66.60 for MixGRPO and 66.32 without MGAI, alongside category-specific weaknesses such as G2RPO's lower Grammar score. Additional visual ablation and generation examples are also reported.

T1.justification: The main mathematical formulation is retained, while Section 11 adds a sampling-step count and overhead derivation. Its numerical example is inconsistent: the printed sums for M = {16, ..., 9} yield 179 total steps and approximately 44.1% under its defined overhead ratio, rather than the reported 184 and 45.7%.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that single-step stochastic exploration improves reward attribution and that multi-granularity advantage integration improves alignment and robustness. Retitling and removing the separate superior-performance contribution bullet do not change these claims, which remain in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: Sections 7–8 add substantive explanations linking single-granularity optimization to reward-model overfitting, domain collapse and structural weaknesses, and argue that VLM metrics better reveal MGAI's benefits. Section 11 newly acknowledges additional training-time sampling cost while claiming unchanged inference latency. These extend v1's more general robustness and reward-hacking discussion.

D1.justification: Table 4 adds warmup, dataloader-worker, gradient-norm, scheduler-shift and policy-clipping details, and the front-page repository link becomes a project-page link. Conversely, v3 omits v1's explicit 300 training iterations and 1024-by-1024, 50-step main inference settings. These are documentation changes, not established changes to execution.

R1.justification: v3 adds the UniGenBench++ citation, explains its decision not to evaluate Flow-GRPO, and removes the assertion that OpenAI o1 adopts GRPO while retaining its citation elsewhere. The broader positioning relative to diffusion alignment, DanceGRPO and MixGRPO remains intact.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, several explanatory passages expand, Preliminary becomes a method subsection, and supplementary material is organized after the references. Much of the main narrative remains closely matched, so the language and organizational revision is limited despite the larger visual redesign.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main paper from single-column to two-column layout, moves Figure 1 before the abstract, revises Figure 2's rendering and compresses Tables 1–3 with abbreviated headers. It adds Tables 4–5 and Figures 5, 8–11. v1 Figures 5–6 are retained as v3 Figures 6–7, and the new galleries include some redisplayed examples.

improvement.justification: The added UniGenBench++ comparison and controlled MGAI visual ablation strengthen evidence beyond v1's reward-score evaluations, while Table 4 improves implementation transparency. These gains are tempered by omitted training and inference details and the inconsistent computational-cost example in Section 11. With the core method and original quantitative results unchanged, the net improvement is useful but limited.
